decisions.reason: As a close-to-core carpet in a firm with a broad assortment and no visible sign of failure yet, it would likely be retained while management waits for clearer market feedback, though overlap with other new carpets raises some pruning risk.
Its premium hand-knotted wool-silk positioning fits the firm's craftsmanship and design identity, so absent clear underperformance management would likely keep it despite its niche demand profile.

This product is near the existing offer and benefits from organisational slack, but because it is another similar low-pile decorative carpet launched alongside others its probability of being culled is somewhat higher.

The corner bench extends the established furniture range and supports residential and project business, so a German furniture maker of this type would usually keep it unless early sales clearly miss aspirations.

Management would probably continue this close-to-core carpet for now, but among the launches it faces relatively high drop risk because several similar carpet introductions make comparison-based aspiration shortfalls more likely.
